author.name: Henry Bushnell
author.description: Henry Bushnell is a senior writer for The Athletic covering soccer. He previously covered a variety of sports and events, including World Cups and Olympics, for Yahoo Sports. He is based in Washington, D.C.

author.name: Adam Crafton
author.description: Adam Crafton is a British journalist based in New York City, having relocated from London in 2024. He primarily covers soccer for The Athletic. In 2024, he was named the Sports Writer of the Year by the Sports' Journalist Association, after winning the Young Sports Writer of the Year award in 2018.

author.name: Paul Tenorio
author.description: Paul Tenorio is a senior writer for The Athletic who covers soccer. He has previously written for the Washington Post, the Orlando Sentinel, FourFourTwo, ESPN and MLSsoccer.com.

author.name: Nick Miller
author.description: Nick Miller is a football writer for the Athletic and the Totally Football Show. He previously worked as a freelancer for the Guardian, ESPN and Eurosport, plus anyone else who would have him.

author.name: Chris Weatherspoon
author.description: Chris Weatherspoon is a Football Finance Writer for The Athletic UK. A chartered accountant, he has previously covered the business of sport on a freelance basis, spanning deep dives into individual club accounts and broader analyses of industry-wide trends and issues, and utilises data and financial acumen to explore the money behind the game.

author.name: Greg O'Keeffe
author.description:
Greg O'Keeffe is a senior writer for The Athletic covering US soccer players in the UK & Europe.
Previously he spent a decade at the Liverpool Echo covering news and features before an eight-year stint as the paper's Everton correspondent; giving readers the inside track on Goodison Park, a remit he later reprised at The Athletic.
He has also worked as a news and sport journalist for the BBC and hosts a podcast in his spare time.

author.name: Steve Madeley
author.description: Steve Madeley has been a journalist for almost 25 years, including nearly 20 years covering sport, mainly football. The majority of his career was spent with the Express & Star in the West Midlands. He has worked for most UK national newspapers and websites including The Times, The Mirror and BBC Sport Online and joined The Athletic in 2019.

author.name: Jack Lang
author.description: Jack Lang is a staff writer for The Athletic, covering football.

author.name: Jessica Hopkins
author.description: Jessica Hopkins is a Staff News Editor at The Athletic. She previously contributed to features and investigations across cycling, athletics and football.

author.name: Colin Millar
author.description: Colin Millar is a Senior Editor for The Athletic. Prior to joining The Athletic, Colin was European Football writer at Mirror Football. From Belfast, he is the author of The Frying Pan of Spain: Sevilla vs Real Betis, Spain’s Hottest Football Rivalry, and he can be found on Twitter/X: @Millar_Colin

author.name: Eduardo Tansley
author.description: Eduardo Tansley is an Explainer Journalist for The Athletic. He completed his postgraduate in Sports Journalism from St Mary's University, Twickenham

author.name: Dan Sheldon
author.description: Dan Sheldon is a football news correspondent for The Athletic. He has previously covered Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea and Southampton FC.

author.name: Mark Carey
author.description: Mark Carey is a Data Analyst for The Athletic. With his background in research and analytics, he will look to provide data-driven insight across the football world.

author.name: Thom Harris
author.description: Thom Harris is a football data writer at The Athletic, with particular interest in data analysis and visualisation. Born and bred on the blue side of Manchester, he is also passionate about the Spanish game, having spent time working for Villarreal C.F in the past.

author.name: Elias Burke
author.description: Elias Burke is a football writer who regularly covers Tottenham Hotspur. He has previously covered U.S. soccer, West Bromwich Albion and Derby County for The Athletic.

author.name: Will Jeanes
author.description: Will Jeanes is a senior editor at The Athletic.

author.name: Matt Slater
author.description: Based in North West England, Matt Slater is a senior sports news reporter for The Athletic UK. Before that, he spent 16 years with the BBC and then three years as chief sports reporter for the UK/Ireland's main news agency, PA.

author.name: Felipe Cardenas
author.description: Felipe Cardenas is a senior writer for The Athletic who covers soccer in South America, North America and more.

author.name: Michael Cox
author.description: Michael Cox concentrates on tactical analysis. He is the author of two books - The Mixer, about the tactical evolution of the Premier League, and Zonal Marking, about footballing philosophies across Europe.

author.name: Melanie Anzidei
author.description: Melanie Anzidei is a Staff Writer for The Athletic covering soccer. Before joining The Athletic, she was an enterprise sports reporter for The Record newspaper and NorthJersey.com, where she was for nearly a decade. She’s a graduate of Columbia Journalism School in New York City.

author.name: Oliver Kay
author.description: Before joining The Athletic as a senior writer in 2019, Oliver Kay spent 19 years working for The Times, the last ten of them as chief football correspondent. He is the author of the award-winning book Forever Young: The Story of Adrian Doherty, Football’s Lost Genius.

author.name: Tim Spiers
author.description: Tim Spiers is a football journalist for The Athletic, based in London. He joined in 2019 having previously worked at the Express & Star in Wolverhampton.

author.name: Matt Woosnam
author.description: Matt Woosnam is the Crystal Palace writer for The Athletic. He also covers topics surrounding climate and environmental sustainability in sport. Matt previously worked as a freelance writer for the South London Press and MailOnline.

author.description: Jack Pitt-Brooke is a football journalist for The Athletic based in London. He joined in 2019 after nine years at The Independent.

author.name: Greg O'Keeffe
author.description:
Greg O'Keeffe is a senior writer for The Athletic covering US soccer players in the UK & Europe.
Previously he spent a decade at the Liverpool Echo covering news and features before an eight-year stint as the paper's Everton correspondent; giving readers the inside track on Goodison Park, a remit he later reprised at The Athletic.
He has also worked as a news and sport journalist for the BBC and hosts a podcast in his spare time.

author.name: Joshua Kloke
author.description: Joshua Kloke is a staff writer who has covered the Maple Leafs and Canadian soccer for The Athletic since 2016. Previously, he was a freelance writer for various publications, including Sports Illustrated.

author.name: Michael Bailey
author.description: Michael Bailey is a senior writer for The Athletic, covering numerous live sports as well hosting of The Athletic FC Tactics Podcast. He hails from the county of Norfolk, previously reporting on Norwich City Football Club for more than 20 years — winning regional and national awards for his coverage.

author.name: Nick Miller
author.description: Nick Miller is a football writer for the Athletic and the Totally Football Show. He previously worked as a freelancer for the Guardian, ESPN and Eurosport, plus anyone else who would have him.

author.name: Tim Spiers
author.description: Tim Spiers is a football journalist for The Athletic, based in London. He joined in 2019 having previously worked at the Express & Star in Wolverhampton.

author.name: Jacob Whitehead
author.description: Jacob Whitehead is a reporter for The Athletic who covers investigations, cycling, and Newcastle United. He previously worked on the news desk. In 2025, he was a Gold Award winner at the 30 to Watch journalism awards.

author.name: Simon Hughes
author.description: Simon Hughes is a senior writer who joined The Athletic from The Independent in 2019. His latest book Chasing Salah was released in 2024. He has also written There She Goes, a modern social history of Liverpool as a city

author.name: Jay Harris
author.description: Jay Harris reports on Tottenham Hotspur for The Athletic. He worked for Sky Sports News for four years before he joined The Athletic in 2021 and spent three seasons covering Brentford. He covered the 2022 World Cup from Qatar and the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations in Ivory Coast.

author.name: Tom Burrows
author.description: Tom Burrows is a football news reporter for The Athletic UK, based in London. He was previously a staff editor for three years. Before that, he worked on news and investigations for national newspapers.

author.name: Dermot Corrigan
author.description: Dermot joined The Athletic in 2020 and has been our main La Liga Correspondent up until now. Irish-born, he has spent more than a decade living in Madrid and writing about Spanish football for ESPN, the UK Independent and the Irish Examiner.

author.name: Jordan Campbell
author.description: Jordan Campbell is a football writer for The Athletic, who regularly covers Manchester City. In 2024, he was named in the 30 to Watch journalism awards. He previously covered Glasgow Rangers and was twice nominated for Young Journalist of the Year at the Scottish Press Awards.

author.name: Conor O'Neill
author.description: Conor is a Data and Tactics Writer for The Athletic. Before joining The Athletic, he worked as a Data Journalist at Sky Sports News for two years, producing analytical features on football and other sports. Conor pivoted into journalism after starting his career in data science and quantitative analysis. He focuses on delivering insightful, engaging, and enjoyable data-driven analysis.

author.name: Colin Millar
author.description: Colin Millar is a Senior Editor for The Athletic. Prior to joining The Athletic, Colin was European Football writer at Mirror Football. From Belfast, he is the author of The Frying Pan of Spain: Sevilla vs Real Betis, Spain’s Hottest Football Rivalry, and he can be found on Twitter/X: @Millar_Colin

author.name: Eduardo Tansley
author.description: Eduardo Tansley is an Explainer Journalist for The Athletic. He completed his postgraduate in Sports Journalism from St Mary's University, Twickenham

## Highlights
  1. ### [David Hockney, Who Restored the Human Form to Art, Dies at 88](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/david-hockney-dead.html)
His colorful figurative paintings were both conservative and iconoclastic, defying the dominant abstract schools of the mid-20th century.
58m agoBy Holland Cotter
![David Hockney’s “Self-Portrait With Red Braces” \(2003\). He remained unfailingly productive almost to the end of his life.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2025/10/14/multimedia/00Hockney--fjwz/00Hockney--fjwz-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![David Hockney’s “Self-Portrait With Red Braces” \(2003\). He remained unfailingly productive almost to the end of his life.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2025/10/14/multimedia/00Hockney--fjwz/00Hockney--fjwz-threeByTwoMediumAt2X.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditDavid Hockney, photograph by Richard Schmidt
  2. An Appraisal
### [What I Learned From David Hockney](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/david-hockney-norman-rosenthal.html)
The curator Norman Rosenthal knew the artist for over 60 years and still discovered something new when they collaborated on a final blockbuster show.
6h agoBy Norman Rosenthal
![Journalists looking at David Hockney’s work before the opening of the exhibition “David Hockney 25” at Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris in April 2025.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/00cul-hockney-appraisal-rosenthal-HFO-mpfc/00cul-hockney-appraisal-rosenthal-HFO-mpfc-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![Journalists looking at David Hockney’s work before the opening of the exhibition “David Hockney 25” at Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris in April 2025.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/00cul-hockney-appraisal-rosenthal-HFO-mpfc/00cul-hockney-appraisal-rosenthal-HFO-mpfc-threeByTwoMediumAt2X.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditDmitry Kostyukov for The New York Times
  3.     1. Anatomy of a Scene
### [Steven Spielberg on How to Build Suspense in ‘Disclosure Day’](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/movies/steven-spielberg-disclosure-day-clip.html)
The director narrates a scene from his movie that is a continuation, of sorts, of a sequence he filmed for his feature-length debut, “Duel,” in 1971.
14h agoBy Mekado Murphy
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/arts/Steven-thumb-horizontal-16x9_6/Steven-thumb-horizontal-16x9_6-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/arts/Steven-thumb-horizontal-16x9_6/Steven-thumb-horizontal-16x9_6-videoLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
Credit
    2. Popcast
### [Slayyyter Had One Last Chance for Pop Stardom, and She Nailed It](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/slayyyter-interview-popcast.html)
After a few attempts that didn’t fully connect, the St. Louis singer was ready to walk away, but not before making a raw album of thrashed pop, “Worst Girl in America.”
14h agoBy Jon CaramanicaJoe Coscarelli and Caroline Tompkins
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/multimedia/12cul-slayyyter-popcast-01-mflt/12cul-slayyyter-popcast-01-mflt-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/multimedia/12cul-slayyyter-popcast-01-mflt/12cul-slayyyter-popcast-01-mflt-videoLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
Credit


  1. [Olivia Rodrigo’s Songs Can’t Always Keep Up With Her Impeccable Taste](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/olivia-rodrigo-you-seem-pretty-sad-for-a-girl-so-in-love-review.html)
On “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love,” the 23-year-old singer delivers a polished, solemn breakup chronicle that misses her signature adrenaline rush.
8h agoBy Lindsay Zoladz
![Olivia Rodrigo’s third album documents a relationship, from beginning to end.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/12cul-rodrigo-review-hqmt/12cul-rodrigo-review-hqmt-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditOK McCausland for The New York Times
Album Review
  2. [Our Critic Frames David Hockney’s Greatest Art](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/david-hockney-partworks-photostack.html)
Whether in Los Angeles, in his native England or traveling the world, the artist always reinvented the world he saw, with psychological insight.
2h agoBy Holland Cotter
![David Hockney, “Portrait of an Artist \(Pool With Two Figures\)” \(1972\), part of a running chronicle of his relationship with his muse, Peter Schlesinger.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/12cul-hockney-photostack-cmwz/12cul-hockney-photostack-cmwz-square640-v2.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditDavid Hockney; Art Gallery of New South Wales 
  3. [With iPhones and Faxes, David Hockney Embraced Tech](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/david-hockney-ipad-iphone-photocopier-fax.html)
Polaroids and photocopiers also gave the artist possibilities for creating in forms vastly different from his paintings.
3h agoBy Alex Marshall
![“Mulholland Drive, June 1986,” a homemade print from a photocopier.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/arts/00cul-hockney-tech-HFO-04/00cul-hockney-tech-HFO-04-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditDavid Hockney
  4. [Opera Company Sues to Collect $17 Million From the Kennedy Center](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/kennedy-center-washington-national-opera-lawsuit-endowment.html)
The Washington National Opera, which left the center amid the Trump administration’s takeover, says its efforts to retrieve its endowment and other assets have been blocked.
8h agoBy Julia Jacobs
![The Kennedy Center and the Washington National Opera are no longer affiliated, but they remained entangled in a dispute over what assets the opera might still be owed. ](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/11/multimedia/11cul-Kennedy-opera-cmlp/11cul-Kennedy-opera-cmlp-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditKenny Holston for The New York Times
  5. [Taylor Swift Enters the Songwriters Hall of Fame With Tears, Jokes and a Warning](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/taylor-swift-songwriters-hall-speech.html)
After an introduction from Steven Spielberg, Swift gave a lengthy speech encouraging artists to “trust their human intuition” in an industry driven by data.
5h agoBy Malia Mendez
![In a speech, Taylor Swift called songwriting “pretty much the only thing I ever just naturally did.”](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/multimedia/12cul-swift-hof3-hjmk/12cul-swift-hof3-hjmk-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditThea Traff for The New York Times


  1. [Review: ‘Romeo & Juliet’ Find Too Little Love in the Park](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/11/theater/review-romeo-juliet-shakespeare-in-the-park.html)
For the Public Theater’s Shakespeare in the Park, the director Saheem Ali presents a strangely low-energy version of the tragedy.
21h agoBy Helen Shaw
![From left, Ra’Mya Latiah Aikens as Juliet, Francis Jue as Friar Lawrence and Daniel Bravo Hernández as Romeo in the play “Romeo and Juliet” at the Delacorte Theater in New York.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/11/multimedia/romeo-juliet-zcqb/romeo-juliet-zcqb-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditSara Krulwich/The New York Times
  2. [Kennedy Center Appeals Order to Remove Trump’s Name](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/11/arts/music/kennedy-center-appeal-trump-name.html)
One day before a deadline to take the president’s name off its facade, the arts institution appealed a federal judge’s ruling that also temporarily blocked it from closing.
10h agoBy Julia Jacobs
![Judge Christopher R. Cooper ruled that only Congress had the power to alter the name of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, which was dedicated to the president in a 1964 law.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/11/multimedia/11cul-kennedy-board-mbzc/11cul-kennedy-board-mbzc-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditKevin Lamarque/Reuters
  3. [The Pianist Igor Levit Bets Big on Recordings With His Own Label](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/igor-levit-no-silence.html)
Despite woes in the recording industry, Levit announced the founding of No Silence, which will release three albums this fall.
14h agoBy Anastasia Tsioulcas
![The pianist Igor Levit, who is partnering with his longtime label, Sony, on the new imprint No Silence.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/12cul-igor-levit-gkct/12cul-igor-levit-gkct-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditJames Estrin/The New York Times
  4. [Conjuring a Mountainous Illusion Out of the Oldest Bridge in Paris](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/pont-neuf-jj.html)
Four decades after the conceptual artist Christo draped the Pont Neuf with fabric, JR, a French street artist, offers his own trick of the eye.
7h agoBy Mark Landler and Elliott Verdier
![The bridge has been wrapped with fabric that was then inflated to create a craggy appearance.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/arts/12cul-pont-neuf-tops/12cul-pont-neuf-tops-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditElliott Verdier for The New York Times
  5. [‘The Gas Station Attendant’: Immigrant Father, Questioning Daughter](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/movies/the-gas-station-attendant-review.html)
Karla Murthy retells her Indian dad’s life story to better understand her own in this deeply personal documentary.
14h agoBy Alissa Wilkinson
![A scene from “The Gas Station Attendant,” about the director’s father, H.N. Shantha Murthy.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/multimedia/12cul-doc-col-kbhp/12cul-doc-col-kbhp-square640-v2.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditGreene Fort Productions

jsonld.transcript: Well, I never felt pressure. No, I always did what I wanted to do. I’ve done what I wanted to do every day. There’s too many bossy boots around. Think they know best, and so on. You’ve got to keep telling them, keep shouting, “But could you do it over there? Not my way.” I prefer bright light so you can see things. And Southern California is wonderful for that. And the colors seem vivid and bright. Therefore, makes you feel better. When I paint, I feel I’m 30. I do, actually. It’s only when I stop, I feel my age.

![Raul Jimenez celebrates scoring Mexico's second goal at the Estadio Azteca. He is jubilant and the crowd wave Mexican flags](https://static01.nyt.com/athletic/uploads/wp/2026/06/12014720/GettyImages-2280463266-1024x683.jpg?width=1920&quality=70&auto=webp)

The 2026 World Cup began Thursday with [eruptions of joy in Mexico City](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7353105/2026/06/11/mexico-world-cup-take-flight/).
At long last — after days, weeks, months, years of controversy over [ticket prices](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7341387/2026/06/08/world-cup-2026-ticket-prices-saga-controversy/), [funding](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7314190/2026/06/11/world-cup-united-states-fifa-cost-investigation/), [visas](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7344372/2026/06/09/infantino-trump-world-cup-visas/) and more — the grandest soccer tournament in human history started with pageantry, emotion and a few great human stories.
Advertisement
In the inaugural match, [Mexico beat South Africa, 2-0](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7352092/2026/06/11/mexico-world-cup-south-africa-quinones-red-cards/). In the nightcap, [South Korea came back to beat the Czech Republic, 2-1](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7352470/2026/06/11/czech-republic-south-korea-empty-seats/). On Friday, attention will shift to Mexico’s co-hosts Canada and the United States; but before we look ahead, Thursday was worth savoring because it reminded us why we love the World Cup.
Throughout the tournament, _The Athletic_ will bring you daily recaps on the World Cup’s biggest talking points and highlight what you shouldn’t miss in the next 24 hours. This is what happened on Matchday 1.

### **Mexico’s timely pick-me-up**
So much of the buildup to this World Cup had revolved around the United States. President Donald Trump [took center stage at December’s draw](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6866496/2025/12/06/world-cup-draw-trump-usa-taste/). U.S. cities bickered with FIFA, soccer’s global governing body and the tournament organisers. American sports [essentially set the ticket market](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6901912/2025/12/19/usa-ticket-prices-sporting-events-world-cup-2026/). Eleven NFL stadiums will host 78 of the 104 matches, including every one from the quarterfinals onward.
Mexico, though, got the opener, and it put on the show that FIFA needed: a _soccer_ show.
Mexico, much more so than its co-hosts, is a soccer country, _una nación futbolera_. It has hosted two men’s World Cups before (1970 and 1986) and, on Thursday, it stopped in its tracks for the third. Streets emptied. Living rooms and the mystical Estadio Azteca filled up. Nerves tingled, then trembled.
And then, in the ninth minute, Julián Quiñones washed away all that tension with the tournament’s first goal, eliciting a nationwide roar. _The Athletic_ ’s Jacob Whitehead [heard it from the streets of Guadalajara](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/mexico-vs-south-africa-live-updates-world-cup-2026-score-result/gPwPUZlCuqXC/RZOjYhmtFvDh/?unlocked_article_code=1.plA.NUnk.8FvV5Y-7fnBJ&source=athletic_user_shared_gift_live_blog_copylink&smid=url-share-ta). Mexican fans across the continent, south and north of the U.S. border, leapt skyward. Inside the stadium, [beer and sombreros flew](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7353105/2026/06/11/mexico-world-cup-take-flight/).

It was the moment Mexico had been waiting for. It was the moment FIFA had been waiting for. It was the moment Quiñones dreamed of when he chose to play for Mexico, and even when he endured xenophobic criticism from some fans who felt that the Colombian-born attacker wasn’t _Mexican enough_.
On Thursday, he became the toast of his adopted country.
Advertisement
Around an hour later, World Cup nerves set in again. Angst gripped the Azteca as Mexico struggled to find a second goal, even after Yaya Sithole received a red card, reducing South Africa to 10 men. (There would be three red cards, two for South Africa and one for Mexico, by the end of the match — making this officially [the dirtiest opening game at a World Cup](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7352942/2026/06/11/world-cup-mexico-south-africa-red-cards/).)

In the 67th minute, though, Raúl Jiménez extinguished all concern, and wrote another remarkable chapter in this opening-day story. You could see it etched across his cracking face. Back in 2020, [Jiménez fractured his skull](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7345463/2026/06/11/raul-jimenez-mexico-world-cup-skull/); his career, it seemed, might be over. Six years later, at age 35, he scored his first World Cup goal.

You could see the emotion instantly, in his fist pumps and his tears. You could see it in teammates’ embraces. You could see it all around the famous stadium, and in the songs that echoed deep into the Mexican night.
It’s what makes the World Cup a peerless event, a national unifier, an enthralling spectacle. The 2026 edition needed only one game to jog the world’s memory.

### **Hydration breaks become commercial breaks**
Perhaps the only stain on Thursday’s curtain-raiser was FIFA’s newly mandated “hydration breaks.” 
Previously, many soccer games have paused in extreme heat; now, irrespective of weather, even indoors, all World Cup matches are pausing for three minutes midway through each half. When [FIFA announced the change](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6871622/2025/12/08/world-cup-2026-hydration-breaks/), it said the breaks were for “player welfare,” but many fans saw through the spin and assumed the breaks would be used by broadcasters to show commercials.
On Thursday, Fox, which holds the English-language U.S. broadcast rights, confirmed those fears.
![](https://static01.nyt.com/athletic/uploads/wp/2026/06/12013714/GettyImages-2281154779-scaled.jpg)
South Korea’s players receive instructions during a hydration break in their win over Czech RepublicLars Baron/Getty Images
It not only cut away to advertisements; during the second half of Mexico-South Africa, [its commercials ran long and caused viewers to miss several seconds of action after play resumed](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6871622/2025/12/08/world-cup-2026-hydration-breaks/).
Advertisement
The blunder sparked an uproar among longtime fans who, for decades, have been accustomed to soccer being a game of two uninterrupted halves. “I hate it,” former U.S. women’s national team star Carli Lloyd [wrote on X](https://x.com/CarliLloyd/status/2065156213604758011?s=20).
The breaks essentially turn soccer into a game of four quarters, à la basketball or American football. They allow coaches to tweak tactics and deliver instructions to players that were once hard to communicate before and after halftime.
On Day 1, the commercials were the main talking point, but the sporting implications will be significant, too. Back in March, Portugal coach Roberto Martinez [predicted](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7159728/2026/03/31/world-cup-hydration-breaks-water-players-coaches-reaction-fifa/): “The game is going to change.”

### **USMNT ‘relaxed’ ahead of glitzy opener**
As one co-host opened the World Cup in style, another, the United States, prepared for its long-awaited moment.
[The U.S. team](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7347138/2026/06/10/world-cup-usmnt-usa-pulisic-guide/), popularly known as the USMNT, will kick off Group D against Paraguay (9pm ET Friday, 2 am BST, Saturday) in Southern California. Years of anticipation, expectation and preparation will collide at SoFi Stadium, an absurdly opulent, $5.5 billion palace. All of it will pile on pressure.
If U.S. players are feeling it, though, they haven’t shown it.
Christian Pulisic, 27, the face of the program since his teenage years, [said Thursday](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7352080/2026/06/11/christian-pulisic-usmnt-world-cup-home/) that he was actually “more relaxed” than he was four years ago, on the eve of the last World Cup.
![](https://static01.nyt.com/athletic/uploads/wp/2026/06/12013906/GettyImages-2280964614-scaled.jpg)
Christian Pulisic will be a key figure for the USMNTJamie Squire/Getty Images
He and his teammates, of course, know that this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to lift American soccer. But they’ve [found strength, comfort and calmness in their togetherness](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7352225/2026/06/11/usmnt-friendship-history-pulisic-adams-mckennie-world-cup/). They seem and sound confident, and so does their coach, Mauricio Pochettino.
Pochettino said at his pre-match news conference that he [would not deliver one last rousing speech](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7352921/2026/06/11/usmnt-paraguay-world-cup-pochettino-speech/) before the opener. “They don’t need any external motivation or an inspirational speech,” he said. His reasoning was simple: it’s a World Cup. “If you are not ready,” he said, “I’m sorry.”
Advertisement
“They need to think tomorrow and play like they are a child,” Pochettino said of his players. “With no pressure, with no responsibility.”

### **Friday’s schedule**
Before the USMNT steps into spotlights, Canada also plays its opener against Bosnia and Herzegovina. That match kicks off at 3 p.m. ET at BMO Field in Toronto.
Canada’s biggest star, Alphonso Davies, [will not play](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7352781/2026/06/11/alphonso-davies-injury-canada-bosnia/) as he continues to recover from a hamstring injury suffered last month. But the Canadians are favored, and are hopeful that they, like the USMNT, can make a run that leaves a lasting impact on soccer in their country.
Then, as 9 p.m. ET approaches, all eyes will turn to the Americans. There are no injuries to report; Chris Richards, the team’s top defender and only question mark over the past few weeks, is available, Pochettino said Thursday.
The only absence of note will be that of President Trump. White House World Cup task force director Andrew Giuliani [confirmed](https://youtu.be/2h-CyrQxYy8?is=5eqbFNYyRZf8mNPu) Thursday that the President [will not attend](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7349265/2026/06/10/donald-trump-usmnt-paragauy-rubio/). He will be the first leader of a host country to skip a men’s World Cup opener in the 21st century. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will lead the U.S. government’s delegation, and will meet with Paraguayan president Santiago Peña.
Both the Canadian and American openers will be preceded by musical performances and ceremonies. And once they conclude, the 2026 World Cup will, finally, be in full swing.
  * **Group B** : Canada vs Bosnia and Herzegovina (3pm ET; 8pm BST)  

  * **Group D** : USA vs Paraguay (9pm ET, Friday; 2am BST, Saturday)

# Television
  1. [What to Watch](https://www.nytimes.com/spotlight/what-to-watch)
  2. [Best of Late Night](https://www.nytimes.com/column/best-of-late-night)
  3. [Saturday Night Live](https://www.nytimes.com/topic/subject/saturday-night-live)


## Highlights
  1. ### [30 Shows to Watch This Summer](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/11/arts/television/summer-tv-shows.html)
“The Bear” serves its last course, “Ted Lasso” gets back on the pitch, and Larry David makes a TV show with the Obamas.
1d agoBy Mike Hale
![“Ted Lasso” returns in August with, center, from left, Brendan Hunt, Jason Sudeikis and Tanya Reynolds.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/arts/11summertv-lasso/11summertv-lasso-thumbLarge-v2.jpg?auto=webp)
![“Ted Lasso” returns in August with, center, from left, Brendan Hunt, Jason Sudeikis and Tanya Reynolds.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/arts/11summertv-lasso/11summertv-lasso-threeByTwoMediumAt2X.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditApple TV
  2. Critic’s Notebook
### [In ‘Widow’s Bay,’ History Is Hard to Kill](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/10/arts/television/widows-bay-review.html)
The season’s best new show is a horror-comedy rooted in a timely idea: Is the past a treasure to preserve or a monster to escape?
3d agoBy James Poniewozik
![Matthew Rhys, left, and Stephen Root play denizens of a quirky, haunted island in “Widow’s Bay.”](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/09/multimedia/widows-gcfj/widows-gcfj-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![Matthew Rhys, left, and Stephen Root play denizens of a quirky, haunted island in “Widow’s Bay.”](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/09/multimedia/widows-gcfj/widows-gcfj-threeByTwoMediumAt2X-v2.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditApple TV
  3.     1. Critic’s Notebook
### [Two Scenes, and Two Very Different Sides of Masculinity](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/06/arts/television/half-man-scenes-masculinity.html)
Powered by exceptional performances from Jamie Bell and Richard Gadd, “Half Man” captures rare moments of male tenderness — before inevitably punishing them.
June 6, 2026By Maya Phillips
![Jamie Bell, left, and Richard Gadd in “Half Man.”](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/08/multimedia/06cul-halfman-notebook-tpvm/06cul-halfman-notebook-tpvm-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![Jamie Bell, left, and Richard Gadd in “Half Man.”](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/08/multimedia/06cul-halfman-notebook-tpvm/06cul-halfman-notebook-tpvm-videoLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditAnne Binckebanck/HBO
    2. ### [How Laverne Cox Slayed Her Demons: With Grit and Glamour](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/10/books/review/laverne-cox-transcendent-memoir.html)
Her memoir follows the path from an abusive childhood to Hollywood stardom. But it’s being released amid a backlash over transgender rights that’s caught up to her, too.
3d agoBy Tim Teeman
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/04/multimedia/00hp-tbr-laverne-cox-kvgj/00hp-tbr-laverne-cox-kvgj-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/04/multimedia/00hp-tbr-laverne-cox-kvgj/00hp-tbr-laverne-cox-kvgj-videoLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditMarcus Maddox for The New York Times


  1. [‘Your Friends & Neighbors’ Wants to Have Its Porsche and Judge It Too](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/05/arts/television/your-friends-neighbors-finale.html)
“We are skewering a value system,” the creator Jonathan Tropper said of the series. “But at the same time, we’re making the show aspirational.”
June 5, 2026By Austin Considine
![Jonathan Tropper left Westchester County, but his experiences in the New York suburb inform his satirical series “Your Friends & Neighbors.”](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/05/multimedia/05cul-tropper-ask-01-zgft/05cul-tropper-ask-01-zgft-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditOK McCausland for The New York Times
Ask a Showrunner
  2. [A First Lady and ‘Absolute Menace’: Maya Rudolph Does ‘Oh, Mary!’](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/10/theater/maya-rudolph-oh-mary-broadway.html)
For her Broadway debut, the comedian hired a trainer, read lines with her daughter and, when she needed it most, was saved by improv.
2d agoBy Alexandra Alter and Thea Traff
![Rudolph’s first thought said about stepping into the role, “was, how do I do what they did?” she said. “I remember saying, I can’t find my voice.”](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/21/multimedia/21CUL-MAYA-RUDOLPH-02-wplz/21CUL-MAYA-RUDOLPH-02-wplz-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditThea Traff for The New York Times
  3. [‘Every Year After’ and 8 More Shows to Watch on TV This Week](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/08/arts/television/every-year-after-tv-this-week.html)
The adaptation of a Carley Fortune novel airs and a new season of “Below Deck Mediterranean” begins.
June 8, 2026By Shivani Gonzalez
![Sadie Soverall and Matt Cornett in “Every Year After.”](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/08/multimedia/8cul-tvcol-every-hkmv/8cul-tvcol-every-hkmv-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditJustine Yeung/Prime
  4. [‘Euphoria’ Goes Out With a Whimper](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/01/arts/television/euphoria-season-3-finale-rue.html)
In the end, a show defined by its excesses seemed to be straining for a redemption that it didn’t need.
June 1, 2026By Mike Hale
![Rue \(Zendaya\) has been the guide and moral center of “Euphoria” from the beginning.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/03/arts/01euphoria/01euphoria-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditEddy Chen/HBO
critic’s notebook
  5. [Why ‘Euphoria’ Had to End This Way. For Good.](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/01/arts/television/popcast-euphoria-sam-levinson-interview.html)
In an exclusive interview, Sam Levinson explained why he felt it was time to bring the series to a close and responded to its detractors.
12h agoBy Joe CoscarelliJon Caramanica and Caroline Tompkins
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/02/multimedia/01cul-levinson-popcast/01cul-levinson-popcast-06-fbwp-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditCaroline Tompkins for The New York Times
Popcast

### [Joe Negri, Handyman and Music Maestro on ‘Mister Rogers,’ Dies at 99](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/joe-negri-dead.html)
An accomplished jazz guitarist, he appeared on more than 300 episodes of the public television show, playing alongside musicians like Wynton Marsalis and Yo-Yo Ma.
By Michael S. Rosenwald
June 12, 2026
  2. ![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/arts/12latenight/12latenight-square320.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
Late Night ROUNDUP
### [Late Night Prepares for Trump’s U.F.C. Birthday Fight at the White House](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/television/late-night-trump-birthday-ufc.html)
Jimmy Fallon called the president “the only 80-year-old yelling, ‘Get on my lawn!’”
By Trish Bendix
June 12, 2026
  3. ![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/14/multimedia/12ST-VOWS-DWTS-01-bqtf/12ST-VOWS-DWTS-01-bqtf-square320.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
Vows
### [A ‘Love Island’ Favorite Finds the Real Thing on ‘Dancing With the Stars’](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/style/laura-nolan-matthew-macnabb-wedding.html)
Laura Nolan developed a crush on Matthew MacNabb when he was on “Love Island UK.” Then they became dance partners on another show.
By Rosalie R. Radomsky
June 12, 2026
  4. ![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/11/arts/11latenight-1/11latenight-1-square320.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
Late Night ROUNDUP
### [Desi Lydic Does a Spit Take at the Price of Trump’s Gold Coin](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/11/arts/television/late-night-desi-lydic-trump-coin.html)
“$12,000? For a coin? Does it come with a used Honda Civic?” Lydic said.
By Trish Bendix
June 11, 2026
  5. ![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/10/multimedia/10Chambers-03-mbqz/10Chambers-03-mbqz-square320.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
### [Ernest Chambers, ‘Smothers Brothers’ TV Show Producer, Dies at 97](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/10/arts/television/ernest-chambers-dead.html)
In the late 1960s, he and Saul Ilson oversaw a variety show known for its social and political satire, and together they helped fight network censors over its content.
By Richard Sandomir
June 10, 2026
  6. ![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/10/arts/10latenight/10latenight-square320.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
Late Night ROUNDUP
### [Jimmy Kimmel Calls a Technical Foul on Trump’s Apparent Game 3 Nap](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/10/arts/television/late-night-trump-nba-finals.html)
The late night host called Trump “the first sitting president to shut down a major United States city so he could take a nap in front of a sold-out crowd at the N.B.A. finals.”
By Trish Bendix
June 10, 2026
  7. ![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/09/arts/09latenight/09latenight-square320.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
Late Night ROUNDUP
### [Late Night Roasts Trump for Walking Out on ‘Meet the Press’](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/09/arts/television/late-night-jon-stewart-trump-meet-the-press.html)
Jon Stewart called the president’s interview his “worst nightmare: a woman who won’t stop asking pertinent questions.”
By Trish Bendix
June 9, 2026
  8. ![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/08/multimedia/08cul-tonys-best-worst-wvbm/08cul-tonys-best-worst-wvbm-square320.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
### [Best and Worst Moments From the 2026 Tony Awards](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/08/theater/best-worst-tony-awards.html)
Pink brought sincerity and high energy as the host, musical numbers by “Cats,” “Ragtime” and “Chicago” popped, and Maya Rudolph and Cole Escola mined comic gold.
By The New York Times
June 8, 2026
  9. ![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/07/multimedia/07xp-pelley-takeaways-hhwa/07xp-pelley-takeaways-hhwa-square320.png?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
### [5 Takeaways From Scott Pelley’s Interview With The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/07/arts/television/scott-pelley-60-minutes-interview-takeaways.html)
Mr. Pelley, who was at CBS News for 37 years, including as a White House correspondent and a “60 Minutes” correspondent, spoke in his first extended interview since he was fired.
By Adeel Hassan
June 7, 2026
  10. ![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/07/multimedia/07tonys-how-to-watch-jbzm/07tonys-how-to-watch-jbzm-square320.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
### [How to Watch the 2026 Tony Awards](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/07/theater/how-to-watch-tony-awards-2026-streaming.html)
The ceremony, at Radio City Music Hall, will be broadcast on CBS starting at 8 p.m. Eastern, and livestreamed on Paramount+ for premium subscribers.
By Michael Paulson
June 7, 2026

## Highlights
  1. ### [David Hockney, Who Restored the Human Form to Art, Dies at 88](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/david-hockney-dead.html)
His colorful figurative paintings were both conservative and iconoclastic, defying the dominant abstract schools of the mid-20th century.
58m agoBy Holland Cotter
![David Hockney’s “Self-Portrait With Red Braces” \(2003\). He remained unfailingly productive almost to the end of his life.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2025/10/14/multimedia/00Hockney--fjwz/00Hockney--fjwz-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![David Hockney’s “Self-Portrait With Red Braces” \(2003\). He remained unfailingly productive almost to the end of his life.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2025/10/14/multimedia/00Hockney--fjwz/00Hockney--fjwz-threeByTwoMediumAt2X.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditDavid Hockney, photograph by Richard Schmidt
  2. An Appraisal
### [What I Learned From David Hockney](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/david-hockney-norman-rosenthal.html)
The curator Norman Rosenthal knew the artist for over 60 years and still discovered something new when they collaborated on a final blockbuster show.
6h agoBy Norman Rosenthal
![Journalists looking at David Hockney’s work before the opening of the exhibition “David Hockney 25” at Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris in April 2025.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/00cul-hockney-appraisal-rosenthal-HFO-mpfc/00cul-hockney-appraisal-rosenthal-HFO-mpfc-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![Journalists looking at David Hockney’s work before the opening of the exhibition “David Hockney 25” at Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris in April 2025.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/00cul-hockney-appraisal-rosenthal-HFO-mpfc/00cul-hockney-appraisal-rosenthal-HFO-mpfc-threeByTwoMediumAt2X.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditDmitry Kostyukov for The New York Times
  3.     1. Anatomy of a Scene
### [Steven Spielberg on How to Build Suspense in ‘Disclosure Day’](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/movies/steven-spielberg-disclosure-day-clip.html)
The director narrates a scene from his movie that is a continuation, of sorts, of a sequence he filmed for his feature-length debut, “Duel,” in 1971.
14h agoBy Mekado Murphy
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/arts/Steven-thumb-horizontal-16x9_6/Steven-thumb-horizontal-16x9_6-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/arts/Steven-thumb-horizontal-16x9_6/Steven-thumb-horizontal-16x9_6-videoLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
Credit
    2. Popcast
### [Slayyyter Had One Last Chance for Pop Stardom, and She Nailed It](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/slayyyter-interview-popcast.html)
After a few attempts that didn’t fully connect, the St. Louis singer was ready to walk away, but not before making a raw album of thrashed pop, “Worst Girl in America.”
14h agoBy Jon CaramanicaJoe Coscarelli and Caroline Tompkins
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/multimedia/12cul-slayyyter-popcast-01-mflt/12cul-slayyyter-popcast-01-mflt-thumbLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
![](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/multimedia/12cul-slayyyter-popcast-01-mflt/12cul-slayyyter-popcast-01-mflt-videoLarge.jpg?auto=webp)
Credit


  1. [Olivia Rodrigo’s Songs Can’t Always Keep Up With Her Impeccable Taste](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/olivia-rodrigo-you-seem-pretty-sad-for-a-girl-so-in-love-review.html)
On “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love,” the 23-year-old singer delivers a polished, solemn breakup chronicle that misses her signature adrenaline rush.
8h agoBy Lindsay Zoladz
![Olivia Rodrigo’s third album documents a relationship, from beginning to end.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/12cul-rodrigo-review-hqmt/12cul-rodrigo-review-hqmt-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditOK McCausland for The New York Times
Album Review
  2. [Our Critic Frames David Hockney’s Greatest Art](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/david-hockney-partworks-photostack.html)
Whether in Los Angeles, in his native England or traveling the world, the artist always reinvented the world he saw, with psychological insight.
2h agoBy Holland Cotter
![David Hockney, “Portrait of an Artist \(Pool With Two Figures\)” \(1972\), part of a running chronicle of his relationship with his muse, Peter Schlesinger.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/12cul-hockney-photostack-cmwz/12cul-hockney-photostack-cmwz-square640-v2.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditDavid Hockney; Art Gallery of New South Wales 
  3. [With iPhones and Faxes, David Hockney Embraced Tech](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/david-hockney-ipad-iphone-photocopier-fax.html)
Polaroids and photocopiers also gave the artist possibilities for creating in forms vastly different from his paintings.
3h agoBy Alex Marshall
![“Mulholland Drive, June 1986,” a homemade print from a photocopier.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/arts/00cul-hockney-tech-HFO-04/00cul-hockney-tech-HFO-04-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditDavid Hockney
  4. [Opera Company Sues to Collect $17 Million From the Kennedy Center](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/kennedy-center-washington-national-opera-lawsuit-endowment.html)
The Washington National Opera, which left the center amid the Trump administration’s takeover, says its efforts to retrieve its endowment and other assets have been blocked.
8h agoBy Julia Jacobs
![The Kennedy Center and the Washington National Opera are no longer affiliated, but they remained entangled in a dispute over what assets the opera might still be owed. ](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/11/multimedia/11cul-Kennedy-opera-cmlp/11cul-Kennedy-opera-cmlp-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditKenny Holston for The New York Times
  5. [Taylor Swift Enters the Songwriters Hall of Fame With Tears, Jokes and a Warning](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/taylor-swift-songwriters-hall-speech.html)
After an introduction from Steven Spielberg, Swift gave a lengthy speech encouraging artists to “trust their human intuition” in an industry driven by data.
5h agoBy Malia Mendez
![In a speech, Taylor Swift called songwriting “pretty much the only thing I ever just naturally did.”](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/multimedia/12cul-swift-hof3-hjmk/12cul-swift-hof3-hjmk-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditThea Traff for The New York Times


  1. [Review: ‘Romeo & Juliet’ Find Too Little Love in the Park](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/11/theater/review-romeo-juliet-shakespeare-in-the-park.html)
For the Public Theater’s Shakespeare in the Park, the director Saheem Ali presents a strangely low-energy version of the tragedy.
21h agoBy Helen Shaw
![From left, Ra’Mya Latiah Aikens as Juliet, Francis Jue as Friar Lawrence and Daniel Bravo Hernández as Romeo in the play “Romeo and Juliet” at the Delacorte Theater in New York.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/11/multimedia/romeo-juliet-zcqb/romeo-juliet-zcqb-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditSara Krulwich/The New York Times
  2. [Kennedy Center Appeals Order to Remove Trump’s Name](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/11/arts/music/kennedy-center-appeal-trump-name.html)
One day before a deadline to take the president’s name off its facade, the arts institution appealed a federal judge’s ruling that also temporarily blocked it from closing.
10h agoBy Julia Jacobs
![Judge Christopher R. Cooper ruled that only Congress had the power to alter the name of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, which was dedicated to the president in a 1964 law.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/11/multimedia/11cul-kennedy-board-mbzc/11cul-kennedy-board-mbzc-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditKevin Lamarque/Reuters
  3. [The Pianist Igor Levit Bets Big on Recordings With His Own Label](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/music/igor-levit-no-silence.html)
Despite woes in the recording industry, Levit announced the founding of No Silence, which will release three albums this fall.
14h agoBy Anastasia Tsioulcas
![The pianist Igor Levit, who is partnering with his longtime label, Sony, on the new imprint No Silence.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/13/multimedia/12cul-igor-levit-gkct/12cul-igor-levit-gkct-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditJames Estrin/The New York Times
  4. [Conjuring a Mountainous Illusion Out of the Oldest Bridge in Paris](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/pont-neuf-jj.html)
Four decades after the conceptual artist Christo draped the Pont Neuf with fabric, JR, a French street artist, offers his own trick of the eye.
7h agoBy Mark Landler and Elliott Verdier
![The bridge has been wrapped with fabric that was then inflated to create a craggy appearance.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/arts/12cul-pont-neuf-tops/12cul-pont-neuf-tops-square640.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditElliott Verdier for The New York Times
  5. [‘The Gas Station Attendant’: Immigrant Father, Questioning Daughter](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/movies/the-gas-station-attendant-review.html)
Karla Murthy retells her Indian dad’s life story to better understand her own in this deeply personal documentary.
14h agoBy Alissa Wilkinson
![A scene from “The Gas Station Attendant,” about the director’s father, H.N. Shantha Murthy.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/06/12/multimedia/12cul-doc-col-kbhp/12cul-doc-col-kbhp-square640-v2.jpg?auto=webp)
CreditGreene Fort Productions

jsonld.transcript: Well, I never felt pressure. No, I always did what I wanted to do. I’ve done what I wanted to do every day. There’s too many bossy boots around. Think they know best, and so on. You’ve got to keep telling them, keep shouting, “But could you do it over there? Not my way.” I prefer bright light so you can see things. And Southern California is wonderful for that. And the colors seem vivid and bright. Therefore, makes you feel better. When I paint, I feel I’m 30. I do, actually. It’s only when I stop, I feel my age.

## Highlights
  1. ### [David Hockney, Who Restored the Human Form to Art, Dies at 88](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/12/arts/design/david-hockney-dead.html)
His colorful figurative paintings were both conservative and iconoclastic, defying the dominant abstract schools of the mid-20th century.

jsonld.transcript: Well, I never felt pressure. No, I always did what I wanted to do. I’ve done what I wanted to do every day. There’s too many bossy boots around. Think they know best, and so on. You’ve got to keep telling them, keep shouting, “But could you do it over there? Not my way.” I prefer bright light so you can see things. And Southern California is wonderful for that. And the colors seem vivid and bright. Therefore, makes you feel better. When I paint, I feel I’m 30. I do, actually. It’s only when I stop, I feel my age.
